available_assertion.objects: CM triples with labelled maximal O_F action and cyclic N subgroup; labelled supersingular triples and optimal O_F embeddings; Pic(O_F) acts on both. The target uses the pointwise centralizer F^times.
available_assertion.hypotheses: F is imaginary quadratic with units ±1; q=ell_0 is odd, inert and unramified in F; (N,q disc(F))=1 and every prime of N splits in F. Retain CM ideal reciprocity, good reduction and specialization, and the separate geometric/Tate-lattice description of enhanced supersingular curves with Frobenius compatibility.
available_assertion.quantifiers: For every ideal class, with one fixed CM type, reduction place and orientation tuple; restriction to each underlying supersingular pair preserves the bijection on its fiber.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Maximal order and conductor one only; arbitrary split prime-power level including powers of2, and odd inert q including3 when the stated hypotheses hold.
available_assertion.uniformity: Multiplicity one for each component. One fixed L, parametrization and additive lambda_M are used for the whole finite class-group sum.
available_assertion.constants: No division by the class-group size. The later stabilizer factor1/2 and coefficient mass are separate arguments.
available_assertion.normalizations: Use the same Artin action on CM points and ideal quotients. Simultaneously inverting the class labels leaves the quadratic-character sum unchanged. Keep the two q-residue orientations distinct.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: The opposite q orientation is obtained by Frobenius or conjugate CM type, not as the image of the same fixed-type reduction. The map to unlabelled curves need not be injective. Extra quadratic units are excluded.
available_assertion.limit_order: Fix the place and actual reference CM point before reducing all classes. Prove the labelled target torsor without assuming reduction surjectivity, then use prime-to-Nq ideal representatives to prove equivariance.
